doc: Target sidecar of the M3 Go extraction (I67 = I38a; fixed at the I67 prereg; contract: rules Y1 and Y2 of the docstring of tests_m3/test_go_loop.py). config_version holon-go-frontend/0.2 is 0.1 plus the additive loop_bodies section (one iteration of each counted loop as loop-free paths over its symbolic induction variable). One document, morph_blob, holds common/batch and common/blob together, so that the clones of one function in the two packages are ops of one Go-op component (spec/M3/lib/go_ops.json). The source tree, the primitives and the limits are spec/M2/lib/go_frontend.json's, verbatim. `holon extract go --milestone M3` writes spec/M3/facts/morph_blob.go.extracted.json from this file; G1 re-extracts and compares it, since spec/M3/lib/link.json exists (holon.gate).

github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/common.B.text: BytesToHash(b) is the 32-byte array holding b right-aligned (common/types.go: SetBytes crops b to its last 32 bytes, then copies it to h[32-len(b):]); for len(b) == 32 element k is b[k].

github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/crypto.K.text: Keccak256Hash(data...) is the keccak-256 digest of the concatenated arguments: an opaque HASH sink; it reads its arguments and retains none of them.

(github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/common..text: Hash.Bytes() has a value receiver and returns h[:], a 32-byte slice over the receiver's copy: a fresh backing array whose element k is h[k].
